 For the Appellant : Mr. Sanjay Kumar Chamaria, Advocate
 For the State : None
Order No. 06/ Dated: 03rd December, 2025 I.A. No. 10575 of 2025 Heard Mr. Sanjay Kumar Chamaria, learned counsel for the appellant.
None appears on behalf of the State.
2. This application has been preferred on behalf of appellant for grant of bail to him, during the pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 363, 376(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 6(1) of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years along with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- for the offence under Section 6(1) of the POCSO Act.
4. It has been alleged that the appellant had enticed away the daughter of the informant for the purposes of marriage.

5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant while referring to the evidence of the victim who has been examined as P.W.-3 that she was known to the appellant for the last three years and there was a love-affair between them.

It has further been submitted that the appellant was all along on bail during trial and the medical report does not support the factum of the victim being pregnant nor the victim has stated so in her evidence.

sentences.text: 6. The victim has been examined as P.W.-3 and she has categorically stated about the establishment of physical relationship with her by the appellant on the pretext of marriage as a result of which she had become pregnant, though, the pregnancy was subsequently terminated.
7. The date of birth of the victim is 01.01.2005 and incident had taken place on 05.01.2022 which would mean that the victim was a minor at the time when the incident had taken place.
The evidence of doctor also clearly reveals that her hymen was found ruptured and the victim was found pregnant.
8. On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail and the prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected.
9. The aforesaid I.A. stand rejected and disposed of.
